title: Link Two Kipping Pull-Ups
subtitle: 2-week focused kipping block
summary: Three short sessions a week for two weeks, built around one skill: once the chin clears the bar, push the bar away and ride straight back into the arch so the second rep starts itself. The clean single is already there — this block removes the reset between reps.

primarySkill.title: The one skill this block trains
primarySkill.cue: Chin over bar → punch the bar away → let the hips swing forward into the arch → rep two starts from the backswing, not from a dead hang.
primarySkill.failureSignal: Dropping straight down under the bar and stopping ends the chain. That descent — not the pull — is the limiter right now.

spacingNote: Prefer non-consecutive days. Keep at least 24h between sessions, and 48h after pull-heavy work.

warmup.title: Warm-up — every session
items: 2×1 box-start push-away descent into one beat swing

sessionRules.title: Rules for every session
items: Cap full unassisted dynamic pull-up reps at 20 per session — every rep is skill practice, not conditioning.
Rest 60–90 seconds between pair attempts. Only fresh attempts count.
Stop pair attempts after two consecutive rhythm misses; finish with assisted patterning or stop for the day.
No butterfly and no toes-to-bar volume during these two weeks.

progressionRule: Move on only when the descent repeats itself: two linked reps with no reset, no chicken-wing pull, and an intact backswing. If the Week 2 quality test does not pass, repeat Week 2 rather than adding reps.

feedbackPrompt.title: Tell Nabu after each session
items: Where the rhythm failed — top, descent, or backswing
Any pain or hand hot spots
Did rep two come from the backswing, or did it need extra arm pull?

weeks.focus: Teach the push-away and the return to the arch, then take a few rested attempts at linking two.

A.label: Find the return
A.goal: Feel the push-away at the top and let it carry you back into the arch.

blocks.note: Hollow to arch, no pull. Set the rhythm you want to keep under the bar.
Pull to chin over bar, punch the bar away, ride the arch. No second pull.
One clean rep flowing straight into two beat swings — never touch a dead hang.
Rest 60–90s. Two consecutive rhythm misses ends the attempts.

notes: Today's session fits after bench press and the box-jump workout only while shoulders, grip, and timing still feel crisp.

Fatigue fallback: if the grip is cooked or the first two pair attempts land late, skip the remaining pair attempts and finish with beat swings and push-away descents only. A tired kip rehearses the wrong descent.

B.label: Consolidate the pair
B.goal: Make today's successful pair repeat with less effort on rep two; do not chase a third rep.

blocks.note: Easy rhythm check. Match the tempo that produced today's successful pairs.

blocks.movement: Box-start push-away descent into two beat swings
blocks.note: Step or jump to chin over bar, actively push the bar away, reach straight arms in the arch, then hold two controlled beat swings. Do not pull back up.
Keep the proven bridge. Let the deliberate return swing lift rep two instead of adding arm force.
Rest 75–90 seconds. Same push-away after rep one; no third-rep attempts tomorrow.

notes: Best placement: immediately after the general/shoulder warm-up, before strength or the metcon.
Do this tomorrow only if at least 24 hours have passed since Session A and shoulders, elbows, grip, and hands feel normal; otherwise move it one day later.
Assistance is unnecessary for this session because both immediate pair attempts succeeded. The aim is a smoother second rep, not a harder pull.

C.label: Remove the reset
C.goal: Shrink the gap between rep one and rep two until it disappears.

blocks.note: Same shapes, same tempo.
The middle swing is the bridge. Push away first, swing second.
Take the middle swing out. Rep two starts off the first backswing.
Only while the timing is still sharp. Stop before it degrades.

weeks.focus: Turn one good pair into a boring, repeatable pair, then test whether it holds on the clock.

A.label: Repeat clean pairs
A.goal: Make the double ordinary — low volume, full rest, same descent every time.

blocks.note: Rhythm check before any pulling.
Reminder reps, not work.
Full rest between sets. Any reset between the two reps ends that set.
Only after the doubles repeat cleanly. Otherwise stop at doubles.

B.label: Make the cadence boring
B.goal: Same timing every rep. The fix is a more repeatable kip, not a bigger one.

blocks.note: Find the tempo you will hold all session.
Minimal assistance, metronome rhythm — three identical descents.
Unassisted, between assisted sets.
Match the assisted cadence exactly.

notes: If a rep only works with a bigger kip, the timing slipped. Take the next attempt slower, not harder.

C.label: Quality test
C.goal: Prove the double repeats under a clock.

blocks.note: Easy. This is a test day, not a volume day.
Two linked reps at the top of each minute, then rest the rest of the minute.
Pass = at least 6 of 8 minutes with two clean linked reps: no reset, no chicken-wing pull, no pain, backswing intact. Otherwise repeat Week 2.

prerequisites.title: Before you start
mustHave: A clean kipping single from a dead hang

repCaps.note: Every session in this block is built to stay under that cap. If a session needs more reps to feel productive, the reps were too easy or the rest was too short.

stopRules: Any torn-hand or hot-spot warning signs
Two consecutive rhythm misses — stop the pair attempts
notes: No butterfly or toes-to-bar work belongs in these two weeks; it dilutes the descent you are trying to fix.
Technique guidance here is not medical advice — your floor coach overrides the app.

m60Scaling.title: Masters (60+) scaling
m60Scaling.intro: Skill practice and workout scaling are different jobs. Keep them separate.
points: Do not rehearse half-kips under fatigue.
In skill work use clean singles or the linked pairs from this block — stop the set the moment the descent goes.
Default WOD substitution: about 40–50% of the programmed reps as strict pull-ups, in small sets, when that preserves the stimulus.
For high-volume or fast metcons, use the coach's intended scale (ring rows, jumping pull-ups, etc.) rather than turning the workout into strict-pull-up failure work.
Never scale 1:1 from kipping reps to strict reps. Ask the floor coach when the intended stimulus is unclear.
During these two weeks keep metcon kipping volume low, so the skill sessions stay the best reps of the week.
